questions.learningObjective: separate three words that share one English gloss by their register and topic

stimulus.body: 下面是一则简短材料，用来考查这一用法的理解。「The word for chatting, since a friendly exchange has no agenda to discuss.」 材料后给出四个选项，只有一个选项与材料本身所提供的信息相符。

questions.stem: 以“separate three words that share one English gloss by their register and topic / Ask whether the talk has a subject matter, or…”为依据核对材料，哪项结论成立？.

options.text: The word for chatting, since a friendly exchange has no agenda to discuss
The word for discussing, since any exchange of views counts as a discussion
options.misconception: treats a casual conversation as though it were a formal discussion

options.text: The word for speaking, since the general verb is always preferred in speech
options.misconception: substitutes a familiar but inapplicable case for the relation the passage establishes

options.text: All three are interchangeable, and the choice between them is only regional
options.misconception: believes register differences in a word set are only matters of place

questions.explanation: The three words divide the work by what the talk is for. The general verb covers simply speaking, and it is what you use when nothing more needs saying. The word for discussing carries a subject matter and a slightly official air, so it turns up in meetings, in the phrase for talking about work, and in reports. The word used in the compound for chatting is reserved for talk whose point is the company rather than the content, which is why it takes a social object instead of a topic. The temptation is to treat all three as synonyms because English uses one short word for the whole range.
questions.hint: Ask whether the talk has a subject matter, or whether the company is the point.

options.misconception: swaps the two while keeping the idea that they name different stretches

options.text: The word for decades, and the word for time in general as a measurable thing
The word for an occasion, and the word for an era of history as a whole
options.misconception: picks an occasion word and an era word instead of the right pair

options.text: The word for an era, and the word for an occasion or a point in time
options.misconception: chooses the two coarsest time words rather than the two wanted

questions.explanation: Four related words are in play and each has its own scale. The word for an occasion names a point or a stretch inside a day, as in at that time. The word for time names the general thing you can spend or lose. The word for decades names a numbered stretch inside a century, so the nineteen-eighties and the nineteen-nineties each take it. The word for an era names a large historical stretch, such as an age of thought or an age of expansion, and it usually carries a judgement. A learner who reaches for the era word when the meaning is a numbered decade has overshot by a whole register.
questions.hint: Ask how wide the stretch of time is, and whether a century can be divided by it.

options.text: Both English words with the same Chinese one, since the language has a single term
options.misconception: substitutes a familiar but inapplicable case for the relation the passage establishes

A learner who assumes a shared shape means a shared meaning reads the second English word straight onto the first Chinese word and produces a sentence about national finances when the intended sentence was about a household budget. The words do look alike in the two languages, which is exactly what makes them a trap rather than an easy pair.

options.misconception: reaches for the sense about distant admiration instead of a marriage

options.misconception: takes the word as English uses the English cognate of it

options.misconception: reads a noun in a noun slot as though a verb had been placed there

questions.learningObjective: identify which part of a written Chinese name is the family name

stimulus.body: 下面是一则简短材料，用来考查这一用法的理解。「The family name comes first, and the given name follows as one or two characters.」 材料后给出四个选项，只有一个选项与材料本身所提供的信息相符。

questions.stem: 本题的关键提示是“identify which part of a written Chinese name is the family name / Ask which part a speaker states first when giving their own…”。哪一项与材料一致？.

options.text: Both halves are given names, and one of them is a courtesy name used in writing
options.misconception: invents a third name function to avoid admitting a family name

options.text: The given name comes first, and the family name is written at the very end
options.misconception: puts the family name last, the way an English name is arranged

options.text: The family name comes last, and the first character is always the given name
options.misconception: mistakes a surface feature of "The family name comes last, and the first…" for the governing rule

options.text: The family name comes first, and the given name follows as one or two characters

questions.explanation: The family name comes first and the given name follows, and the given name is either one character or two, which is why three-character names are the commonest shape of all. The order holds in speech as well as in writing, so a speaker introducing themselves gives the family name first and then the given name, and a foreigner with a two-part name is expected to follow the same order. A small number of family names consist of two characters rather than one, and those are written as one block with no marker, which is a genuine trap for a learner who assumes the first character alone is the family name.
questions.hint: Ask which part a speaker states first when giving their own name aloud.

stimulus.body: 下面是一则简短材料，用来考查这一用法的理解。「One word names an older brother and the other names a younger one, and both are required.」 材料后给出四个选项，只有一个选项与材料本身所提供的信息相符。

options.text: Relational terms are used at all, where English has no word for a brother at all
options.misconception: mistakes a surface feature of "Relational terms are used at all, where…" for the governing rule

options.text: One word covers both, and the age is settled by the tone the speaker uses
options.misconception: believes a single word leaves the older and younger case to intonation

options.text: One word names an older brother and the other names a younger one, and both are required

A learner who uses one word for both loses a distinction that family members themselves rely on, and one who uses the older word for a younger brother has said something that is simply not true.

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.learningObjective: explain why one word names both a grandmother and a much younger stepmother

stimulus.body: 请阅读以下材料：「The word for a grandmother, which on the father's side can also mean a stepmother.」 四个选项中，只有一个能够从材料本身推出。

questions.stem: 以“explain why one word names both a grandmother and a much younger stepmother / Ask whether the two women are in the same…”为依据核对材料，哪项结论成立？.

options.text: The word for a mother, shared by a man's own mother and by his father's wife
options.misconception: moves the ambiguity onto the two women who are a generation apart

options.text: The word for a grandmother, which on the father's side can also mean a stepmother
The word for an aunt, used for any older woman living inside one household
options.misconception: widens the word to a whole category of women in a home

options.text: The word for a wife, used for a grandmother and for a young stepmother alike
options.misconception: reverses the direction of the reasoning the passage sets out

questions.explanation: The word for a grandmother on the father's side does double duty, because in an earlier period a man might marry a woman young enough to be his own age, and from the children's point of view that woman occupies the grandmother's slot. The result is a genuine ambiguity that a speaker resolves by context, and it is a good example of kinship vocabulary recording a social history rather than only a family tree.
questions.hint: Ask whether the two women are in the same generation as each other's children.

options.text: Cutting down on phone use freed several hours of study time each evening

questions.explanation: The topic sentence is the one that could stand alone as a claim, and the test is not whether the sentence sounds important but whether it is true without the others. The first sentence makes a claim that the rest of the paragraph can go on to support, qualify and assess, so it holds on its own. The second sentence is an example, and an example cannot be the whole point because the paragraph is not about drawers. The third sentence narrows the claim by admitting an exception, which is a job for a later sentence, not the opening one. The fourth is a closing judgement, and it is the easiest to pick by accident because it sounds like the conclusion of an argument and a learner who has been trained to look for the strongest claim at the end of a paragraph will reach for it. options.misconception: chooses a concession that these two sentences do not actually set up

options.text: 但是 (but), which sets the second point against the first
options.misconception: picks the contrastive connective when the second point is meant to strengthen the first

options.text: 所以 (therefore), which draws the second point out of the first as a result
options.misconception: reads an added support as a conclusion drawn from what came before

options.text: 而且 (moreover), which places the second point beside the first

questions.explanation: The connective carries the relationship, so choosing wrongly is not a slip of vocabulary but a change of meaning, which is why the same two clauses can be joined four ways and produce four different paragraphs. When the second sentence supports the first, the connective has to put the two side by side and let the second add weight, and that is what the additive connective does. The contrastive one is the commonest wrong choice in a learner's writing, because it is the connective they meet first in reading and reach for whenever they want to sound decisive, and choosing it here would make the writer's second point argue against the first. The result connective is wrong in the other direction, since it would turn added evidence into a conclusion the paragraph has not earned. The concessive one needs a pair of clauses in which the first is a point that gets taken back, and that is not the pair described here.
questions.hint: Decide first what the two sentences do to each other, and only then name the connective.

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.learningObjective: state what a summary must keep and what it may leave out

stimulus.body: 请阅读以下材料：「A summary has to keep the claim and drop the evidence, and the mistake in the learner's sentence is almost certainly that it dropped one of the claims instead of some of the support for a claim.」 四个选项中，只有一个能够从材料本身推出。

questions.stem: 本题的关键提示是“state what a summary must keep and what it may leave out / Ask what the original four sentences were for, and which of their…”。哪一项与材料一致？.

answer.exemplar: A summary has to keep the claim and drop the evidence, and the mistake in the learner's sentence is almost certainly that it dropped one of the claims instead of some of the support for a claim. Start by asking what the original is for. If four sentences about a community garden are there to report an outcome, the outcome is the claim: the plot was cleared and turned into beds, fewer people came than had signed up, and the harvest was shared in August. That outcome is what a one-sentence version must still say, including the part that went badly, because dropping the disappointing number does not make the summary tidier, it makes it untrue. A summary is allowed to leave out the individual names, the dates of each work day, the price of the timber and the arguments about where to put the water butt, because none of those is what the passage concludes. It is also allowed to compress a list into a category, so a paragraph that names six vegetables becomes a sentence that says home-grown vegetables. What it is not allowed to do is settle a dispute the original left open, sharpen a tendency into a fact, or add a reason the original never gave, and those three additions are what a learner most often makes by accident when shortening a passage, because joining things up is easier than leaving them loose. A good check is to put the original and the summary side by side and ask whether a reader who had seen only the summary would be misled about anything. If the answer is no, the sentence is short enough and the claim has survived.

questions.explanation: This item asks a learner to teach the principle rather than apply it once, because the principle is what makes a later judgement possible. Learners who can shorten a passage usually cannot yet say why one shortening works and another does not, and the reason is that they are thinking about length rather than about claim. Framing the work as claim versus evidence makes the two halves of the task separable: the claim must survive, the evidence is free to go. Naming the three additions that summaries most often smuggle in, a settled dispute, a sharpened tendency, an invented reason, is worth the time it takes, because those are the failures that survive a careful reading and turn up later as a misreading of the source.
questions.hint: Ask what the original four sentences were for, and which of their words a reader would need in order to know that.

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.learningObjective: choose a register for a translation and then rewrite in it

stimulus.body: 请阅读以下材料：「Stage one: the choice is a polite, written register, the one a business uses with somebody it does not know yet.」 四个选项中，只有一个能够从材料本身推出。

questions.stem: 以“choose a register for a translation and then rewrite in it / Ask who wrote the message, who reads it, and whether the two have…”为依据核对材料，哪项结论成立？.

answer.exemplar: Stage one: the choice is a polite, written register, the one a business uses with somebody it does not know yet. The deciding facts are all in the situation rather than in the words. A first-time contact means the relationship has not been established, so the marker of respect has to be there; a customer means the sender is the one who wants something, so the message cannot sound like a note between equals; and two hard facts, a posting date and a delivery window, mean the sentence is transactional and the politeness has to be carried by the wording around the facts rather than by the facts themselves. A learner who answers casual here has picked the register of a friend rather than the register of a supplier, and the message will read as either rude or careless, depending on how much the recipient likes being a customer. Stage two: one sentence that keeps both facts and holds the register is 您好，您的订单已于昨日寄出，预计三个工作日内送达。 The posted date is in the middle, stated as a completed fact; the window follows as an estimate, with the expected word marking it as a promise about a range rather than a guarantee; and the opening word marks the respect before any content arrives. A version that keeps the same two facts but reads like a text message to a friend drops the respect marker and shortens the window, and a version that keeps the respect marker but adds an apology the original never contained has translated the relationship as well as the message, which is a different mistake. The check that catches both is to read the sentence twice, once as the sender and once as the customer, and ask whether each reading finds anything the other did not put there.

questions.explanation: The two stages test different things and the pairing is the point. Choosing a register is a judgement about a relationship, and a learner can usually do it if asked directly. Writing in that register is a production task that exposes every gap in the judgement, because the words available in the chosen register do not line up one for one with the words in the source, and a learner who has only ever named registers will freeze at that point. The pairing also keeps the content honest, since both stages insist on the same two facts, so a fluent rewrite cannot be rewarded for quietly dropping the delivery window, which is the most common way a learner improves a sentence without improving the message.
questions.hint: Ask who wrote the message, who reads it, and whether the two have spoken before, then build the sentence around the two facts.
